key_insight: StudentBench shows that AI tutoring can produce learning gains on GRE-style tasks that are equivalent to human tutoring. The paper shifts the question from “can LLMs answer well?” to “can LLMs help people learn as effectively as humans?”
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of scalable, real-world evaluation methods for measuring whether AI tutors improve student learning as much as human tutors do. It also tackles the shortage of large-scale data on student-AI interactions for educational assessment.
method: Built StudentBench, a public evaluation platform for AI teaching and tutoring tasks.
Collected over 175,000 student-AI messages to analyze tutoring interactions at scale.
Measured learning gains on GRE-style quantitative tasks and compared AI tutoring against human tutoring.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more meaningful benchmark for educational AI: not just answer quality, but actual learning outcomes. It can guide the development and evaluation of LLM tutors, educational products, and human-AI collaboration systems.

paper_title: StudentBench: AI and human tutoring yield equivalent GRE learning gains
paper_authors: Curtis Northcutt, Inaara Hasmani, Kevin Feng, Trevor Khangi, Andreas Plesner
